chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of our companions, altogether from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Aban, from a man, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There are five (things), if you were to come across these, so seek Refuge with Allah from these – Never has an immorality appeared among a people at all to the extent of it being performed openly except there appeared among them, the plague and the hunger which did not happen to be among their ancestors in the past.'
And never have they (people) been deficient in the measuring and the weighing except that they were seized by the years (of famine), and difficult provision, and tyranny of the ruling authorities;
and never have they (people) prevented the Zakāt except that the drops from the sky were prevented, and had it not been for the beasts, it would not have rained;

and never have they (people) broken the Covenant of Allah and the Covenant of His Rasool except that Allah Caused them to be overcome by their enemies, and they seized part of what was in their hands;
and never have they judged with other than what Allah Mighty and Majestic Sent down except that Allah Mighty and Majestic Made the fear (of battles) to be between them'.

key_terms.الْمِكْيَالُ وَ الْمِيزَانُ: The measure and the weight (trade accuracy)

ai.seo_question: What are the five divine punishments for specific communal sins in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith establishes a causal link between communal moral decay and immediate, tangible divine retribution, a concept central to Shia eschatological and sociological thought. It emphasizes that these punishments are not merely future-oriented but manifest in history through specific calamities like plague, famine, and internal strife, serving as warnings for the Ummah.
